title: Salinity matching retains the North Pacific AOU pattern but does not recover a Southern Hemisphere outcrop relation in 1985-2021
abstract: We test whether water-type change hides an outcrop signal in Southern Hemisphere oxygen change. We directly match salinity in GLODAPv2.2023 spatial cells for 1985-1999 and 2006-2021. We hold the published outcrop predictions fixed and resample cruises jointly across density classes. Across 21 southern gyre-classes, the matched slope is 0.330 with a conditional 95% interval of -0.478 to 1.102. All three planned sensitivity intervals include zero. The North Pacific seven-class pattern remains positive: slope 0.570, interval 0.334 to 0.808. Salinity matching reduces the South Indian mean AOU gain from 3.76 to 0.22 umol/kg, but does not recover the predicted southern class pattern. The North Atlantic mean gain remains 5.26 umol/kg. This does not confirm the prior exploratory global extension. It does not exclude a weak southern effect or show a significant difference between regional slopes. Limits include common-support loss, coarse density classes, fixed whole-gyre predictions, shared source observations and incomplete calibration uncertainty. Code, source hashes, aggregate bootstrap draws and figures are included.
